sketch-0.title: Define a class in its model file
sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
A class can live in the file that owns that model.

```text
models/
  recipe.py
main.py
```

`models/recipe.py`:

```python
class Recipe:
    pass
```

A small class file gives the model a clear home. `main.py` does not need to contain every class definition in the application.

sketch-1.title: Import a class across the file boundary
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
Once the class has its own module, another file imports it before creating objects.

```python
from models.recipe import Recipe

breakfast = Recipe()
dinner = Recipe()

print(type(breakfast).__name__)
```

The module path follows the folder and filename: `models/recipe.py` becomes `models.recipe`.

The important boundary is **define the model in its module; import and use it elsewhere**.
